The idea

Nature’s care.
In your day.

From a personal-care routine to family life and an active day, Natoral has room to grow while keeping one recognisable signature.

Natoral is a nature-first brand spanning body care, haircare, baby foods and supplements, and bodybuilding products. This study expands the original identity into a connected family of product names, packaging and everyday imagery.

Design
Eyilade Oridamisi
Scope
Identity extension, naming, packaging & art direction
Portfolio development
Product names, variants and pack sizes are proposed concepts. New photographs and mockups are AI-assisted visualisations with fictional models.

A family, with room to grow

One signature.
Four worlds.

The logo stays constant. Names, clear descriptors and a small colour shift help each range find its place.

The original foundation

A natural gesture.
A distinctive name.

The layered symbol and rounded wordmark are the original work. Deep green, leaf green and the quiet grey signature keep the identity grounded.

A small mark, a wider world

A shape that
holds it together.

The mark’s rounded rhythm becomes a supporting edge, a repeated pattern and a small finishing detail.

The close-up

Care in
the details.

A practical closure. A clear label. A surface that feels tangible. Small decisions give a proposed product a convincing presence.

A familiar name.
A useful object.
A daily ritual.

The same label hierarchy carries from the full range down to a single bottle in someone’s hand.

In the everyday

For quiet moments.
For busy days.

Natural gestures and contemporary spaces give the brand a human scale.

The baby range shown here is a packaging and naming exploration. It does not establish ingredients, doses or age suitability. New product concepts are separate from the original identity work.

A voice for the everyday

A little room
for yourself.

Short, direct messages leave the people, the objects and the original signature space to speak.

Beyond the bottle

A thoughtful
arrival.

A repeated mark inside the pack, a small seal and a personal note. The identity continues through the whole presentation.

The starting point

The original
work.

The supplied identity established the stacked and horizontal signatures, colour variations and repeat pattern. This new study extends that visual language into named product families.

Packaging faces and photographic mockups are portfolio proposals, not approved sale labels. No ingredients, nutrition values, certifications or performance results have been invented.
